question: Should OpenClaw accept Android device-control, ADB-style access, or dynamic code execution from connected Android nodes, and should that be Android-specific commands or part of a generic node-advertised tool contract?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix; it changes phone authority, private-data access, and model-visible execution boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent security/product shape.

options.title: Split and gate Android authority
options.body: Implement only narrow Android device-control commands after explicit permission UX and policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

options.title: Route through node-hosted tools
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/8287 and the candidate PR path as the core contract, then let Android expose only approved descriptors through that model.

options.title: Keep high-power execution out of core
options.body: Reject ADB and dynamic Android code execution in OpenClaw core for now and require external plugins or app-specific forks for that authority.

recommendation.title: Split and gate Android authority
recommendation.body: Implement only narrow Android device-control commands after explicit permission UX and policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current routing signal for the generic node-to-model tool contract is the open candidate PR and recent node/Gateway/tool history under this account.
